title: Keep a weekly class at its time on the gym's clock

blocks.text: A chain of gyms publishes its weekly classes through a public API, which sends each session as an ISO-8601 date-time with an offset, such as `2026-06-03T18:00+10:00`. A class is set up with its first session, a `ZonedDateTime` in the gym's own zone, and meets every week at the same time on that gym's clocks.
Members complain twice a year that the app shows classes an hour off, and the early-morning classes of one gym stayed an hour late for the rest of the season after one night in March.

Finish `sessions` in `src/main/java/practice/WeeklyFeed.java`: the first `count` sessions, starting with the first one. When a session's time doesn't exist that week because the clocks skip it, the session is held at the time the zone moves it to, and the weeks after it are not affected. About five lines in total.

cases.says: with no clock change in between, every session has the first session's time and offset, one week apart
the feed starts with the first session itself
after the zone changes its clocks, sessions keep their local time and carry the zone's new offset
a session whose time is skipped by the clocks moves for that week only; later weeks return to the class's time

origin.section: Spot the Problem: The Weekly Maintenance Window

concepts: An OffsetDateTime keeps the offset it was created with, so calendar arithmetic across a clock change gives the wrong wall-clock time; a ZonedDateTime asks its zone's rules for the new offset.
Stepping each occurrence from the previous one carries a gap's shift into every later week; computing occurrence k from the first confines it to the week of the gap.
